[Thinking]
**Organizing a to-do list**

I'm focusing on creating a structured to-do list with different phases to tackle. I want to include Admin setup, Planning, Daily/Weekly routines, a Content focus checklist, Practice Q targets, a Review/remediation loop, NGN strategies, and Metrics to check readiness. I also need to add a Final week section and a plan for Test day, plus a Plan B if the initial approach doesn't work out. I’ll keep it concise and clear!
[/Thinking]

Here’s a practical, step-by-step NCLEX to-do list you can follow. Adjust timelines to your target test date.

1) Set up the admin basics (Week 0)
- Confirm eligibility with your state board of nursing
- Apply for licensure and register with Pearson VUE
- Watch for your ATT email; schedule your exam date/time and location
- Request accommodations if needed
- Gather valid ID and review test center rules

2) Learn the exam
- Download and read the latest NCSBN NCLEX Test Plan (RN or PN)
- Understand CAT and Next Gen NCLEX (NGN) items: case sets, bow-ties, matrix, trend, cloze, partial credit scoring
- Know the categories: Management of Care, Safety & Infection Control, Health Promotion, Psychosocial, Basic Care & Comfort, Pharmacology/Parenteral Therapies, Reduction of Risk Potential, Physiological Adaptation

3) Do a baseline diagnostic
- Take a 75–100 question mixed practice test (timed)
- Identify top 3 weak areas and top 3 item types you miss (e.g., prioritization, pharm, SATA, NGN case sets)

4) Build a 6–8 week study plan (adjust as needed)
- Daily: 60–120 practice questions + targeted review/remediation
- Content blocks: 1–2 focused topics per day; rotate systems
- 2–3 NGN case sets per day
- Weekly: 1 full-length mixed exam (75–150 Qs), review all rationales
- Rest day: light review only

5) Core resources (pick 1–2, not all)
- Qbanks with strong NGN: UWorld, Archer, SimpleNursing, Kaplan, NCLEX Mastery; NCSBN Learning Extension if available
- Content review: Saunders, SimpleNursing videos, Mark Klimek notes (if you have them), Nurse Achieve (adaptive)
- Labs/normal values cheat sheet; isolation precautions

6) High-yield content checklist
- Safety & Infection Control: isolation, PPE sequence, sterile technique
- Prioritization/Delegation/Triage: ABCs, Maslow, unstable vs stable, scope of practice
- Pharmacology: high-alert meds, adverse effects vs expected, antidotes, IV titration basics
- Med-Surg musts: cardiac (HF, MI), respiratory (asthma/COPD, ABGs), neuro (stroke), renal, endocrine (DKA/HHS, SIADH/DI), GI bleed/pancreatitis
- Maternal-Newborn: stages of labor, fetal monitoring strips, preeclampsia, postpartum care
- Pediatrics: milestones, vaccines, congenital heart defects, dehydration
- Psych: therapeutic communication, priority safety scenarios
- Procedures: chest tubes, trach care, wound/drain care, central lines
- Lab values: CBC, CMP, ABGs, coag, drug levels
- Math: dosage and IV drip rate calculations

7) Daily study routine template
- 10 min: quick review (labs, precautions)
- 60–90 min: mixed Qbank set (timed); flag tough items
- 45–60 min: deep remediation (read rationales for right and wrong answers; make 2–3 takeaway flashcards)
- 20–30 min: NGN practice (case sets/bow-ties)
- 20–30 min: focused content (weak area)
- 10 min: memory refresh (flashcards/Anki)

8) Remediation loop
- Track errors by topic and reason (content gap, misread stem, strategy)
- For each miss, write: key concept, why wrong, how to catch next time
- Re-do flagged questions after 3–5 days for spaced repetition

9) Test-taking strategies
- Identify the priority client using ABCs, safety, unstable, new onset, recent post-op, or changing status
- Eliminate answers that delegate assessment/teaching to UAP or are outside scope
- For pharm, ask: is the effect expected? If severe/abnormal, hold and notify; if mild/expected, monitor/educate
- Read stems for absolute words (always/never) and for safety risks
- For NGN, fill what you know first; partial credit helps—don’t leave blanks

10) Performance targets that suggest readiness
- Consistent Qbank average 55–65%+ on mixed, timed sets
- NGN case set scores improving week-to-week
- Can explain rationales back in your own words
- Weak areas narrowed to 1–2 topics with a plan

11) Final 7-day checklist
- 2–3 light mixed sets per day; heavy remediation days early in the week
- Review: labs, isolation, prioritization/delegation, emergency meds, OB strips, peds milestones
- Do one dress-rehearsal: timed 75–125 Qs, same start time as exam
- Visit test center route/parking; prep ID, snacks, layers
- Sleep routine, hydration, brief exercise

12) Day-before and day-of
- Day-before: no cramming; 25–50 easy questions + quick skim of notes
- Pack ID, ATT, snack, water; know pearson rules; plan to arrive 30 min early
- Test day: eat, breathe, pace; one question at a time; use breaks

13) If you need to retest (just in case)
- Take 48 hours off; request score report/CPR if available
- Identify domains below passing; rebuild plan targeting those
- Switch or refresh Qbank; increase NGN practice; shorten retake window if knowledge is fresh

Optional weekly outline (example for 6 weeks)
- Week 1: Foundations, Safety/IC, Pharm basics; 400–500 Qs total
- Week 2: Cardio/Resp + Prioritization/Delegation; start NGN cases daily
- Week 3: Neuro/Renal/Endocrine; dosage calc practice
- Week 4: GI/MSK/Integ + Psych communication
- Week 5: OB/Peds + Infection control deep dive
- Week 6: Mixed review, weak areas, full-length practice, taper volume

If you tell me your target date, weak areas, and preferred resources, I can turn this into a personalized weekly schedule.
